blocks.text: Data visualization plays an important role in hypothesis testing by presenting data in a clear and understandable form. It helps researchers observe patterns, trends, and relationships in data before applying statistical tests. Visual representations make complex data easier to interpret and reduce the chances of misunderstanding results. Through charts and graphs, differences between groups can be easily compared (as shown in Figure 7.2). Visualization also assists in identifying outliers and anomalies in datasets. It supports better decision-making by providing visual evidence. Overall, data visualization strengthens the process of hypothesis testing by improving clarity and accuracy.

blocks.alt: Four charts in a 2 by 2 grid: a Bar Chart (Value 0 to 100) with a blue Control Group bar and a taller orange Treatment Group bar, each with an error bar; a Line Graph of Value against Time with lines Prediction A and Prediction B; a pie chart of 40%, 15%, 20% and 25%; and a scatter plot of Variable 2 against Variable 1 with blue Group A and orange Group B points, a dashed rising line and two circled points labelled Outlier.
blocks.caption: Figure 7.2: Data Visualization (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 7.2)
blocks.long_description: Bar chart: Control Group about 63 and Treatment Group about 77. Line graph: the blue Prediction A rises steadily; the orange Prediction B rises more slowly and has a flat part marked by two black dots. Scatter plot: Variable 2 runs from 0 to 2; Group A points lie to the left and Group B points to the right of the dashed line.
